title: The Portable Chemical Sterilizer (PCS), D-FENS, and D-FEND ALL: Novel Chlorine Dioxide Decontamination Technologies for the Military
protocol: Place the PCS on a level surface and open the lid.
Place a surgical tray containing clean, non-sterile instruments wrapped in blue autoclave paper on the stilts inside the case.
Mix dry chemicals (e.g., 93 g sodium chlorite, 63 g sodium sulfite, 25 g sodium hydrogen ascorbate) and 300 ml water in the wide-mouthed reaction vessel to initiate chemical reaction.
Close and lock the lid.
Connect a battery-operated or hand-powered air pump to the inlet valve and flow air into the chamber for approximately 5 minutes at 25 min after initiating the reaction.
Open the case and remove the surgical tray of sterile instruments after the cycle completion.
Dispose of the reaction vessel containing water and benign chemical salts.
Place commercially available B/T Sure Biological Indicators inside the case before starting a sterilization cycle.
Remove and activate the indicators after completing the ClO2 sterilization cycle.
Incubate the biological indicators for 24-48 hours to validate sterilization.
Place aqueous suspensions of G. stearothermophilus spores inside the PCS for exposure to a ClO2 sterilization cycle.
Recover G. stearothermophilus spores exposed to the chlorine dioxide treatments on Antibiotic Assay Medium with 1% soluble starch.
Examine refractility of treated spores with phase contrast microscopy.
Inoculate hard, non-porous surfaces made of glass or metal with aqueous suspensions of G. stearothermophilus spores.
Place inoculated materials into the PCS for treatment with a ClO2 sterilization cycle.
Sample the treated surfaces with commercially available Difco HY-Check swabs.
Obtain no-growth to confirm sterility.
Mix 4.7 g sodium chlorite, 1.6 g sodium sulfite, and 1.3 g sodium ascorbate in a small volume.
Dilute the mixture to its final working volume of up to 800 ml to generate an aqueous chlorine dioxide solution with a concentration of 50 − 500 ppm.
Spray the generated chlorine dioxide solution as a fine mist or aerosol onto intended surfaces for disinfection or decontamination.
Allow the chlorine dioxide solution in D-FENS to remain stable for at least 8 hours during a shift.
Empty any remaining solution down sink or floor drains at the end of the shift to purge biofilms.
Prepare Petri dishes of Baird-Parker Agar containing egg yolk tellurite and Yeast Extract.
Inoculate the agar surface with 0.1 ml of a ~106 cfu/ml suspension of a 3-strain cocktail of Staphylococcus aureus.
Spray the porous agar surface with the D-FENS spray bottle containing chlorine dioxide solution.
Dispense approximately equal volumes of solution per spray-trigger pulse.
Rotate the plates 90º between successive pulses to apply uniform coverage of the agar surface.
Use a glass hockey stick and light pressure to spread the chlorine dioxide solution over the agar surface for mechanical abrasion.
Inoculate sterilized stainless steel coupons with 0.2 ml volume of bacterial cell suspensions (e.g., S. aureus, Escherichia coli, or Listeria monocytogenes).
Spread inocula uniformly across the coupon surface.
Air-dry inoculated coupons for 30 min at room temperature in a laminar flow hood.
Immerse inoculated coupons in 20 ml test solution containing chlorine dioxide in a 100 ml stomacher bag.
Quench the sanitizer solution by adding sodium sulfite solid after contact times of 0.5 to 5 min.
Masticate quenched solution for 2 min in a stomacher.
Withdraw supernatant and serially dilute solution onto pre-made agar plates.
Incubate agar plates for 24 hr at appropriate conditions to enumerate survivors.
Inoculate the exterior surfaces of 25 gram samples of tomato wedges with either 105 CFU/g L. monocytogenes OSY-8578 or with 106 CFU/g E. coli ATCC 11229.
Air-dry inoculated tomato wedges in a sterile bio-hood for 15 min.
Place tomato wedges in the PCS after inoculum dries.
Place spore bio-indicators inside the PCS to accompany the tomato wedges and validate sterilization treatment.
Place tomato wedges in a stomacher bag with 50 ml of aqueous phosphate buffer (pH 7).
Masticate for 2 min with a stomacher blender.
Dispense masticated solution as serially 10-fold dilutions onto TSAYE plates for L. monocytogenes and NA plates for E. coli.
Spread the diluted samples on agar plates using a glass hockey stick.
Incubate plates at 35 °C for 24-48 hours.
Enumerate survivors using a colony counter to confirm microbial inactivation.
Place uninoculated apple slices in separate Petri dishes inside the PCS and expose them to chlorine dioxide.
Remove treated apple slices from Petri dishes after treatment.
Expose treated apple slices to ambient environment.
Observe apple slices for visual signs of browning over up to 1 week post-treatment.
Generate aqueous ClO₂ solution by mixing 0.8-3.3 g of reagents in 15-1,200 ml of aqueous solution.
Inoculate sterile strips of textile samples with aqueous suspensions of Bacillus anthracis Sterne or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens spores.
Let the inoculated textile strips air-dry in a laminar flow hood.
Pick up the dried textile strips using sterile forceps and immerse them in 20 ml of chlorine dioxide solution in a 100 ml stomacher bag.
At 10 min, quench the process by adding a small amount of sodium sulfite solid without affecting spores.
Masticate the textile strip and solution for 2 min in a stomacher.
Remove the bag from the stomacher and serially dilute the solution onto pre-made agar plates.
Incubate the agar plates for 24 hr.
Enumerate to validate decontamination.
